title: The Bone Key
text: A key carved from a finger bone hangs on a cord over a barrow's door, turning slowly though there is no wind. The knuckle still has a ring on it. The lock beneath it is shaped like a mouth.

options.label: Put the bone key in the mouth, and see what it swallows.

outcomes.text: The mouth swallows the key. The door opens on a quiet tomb and its treasure.
The door opens on a tomb that was never quiet. Something inside has been waiting for a key.

options.label: The wisest works out whose finger it was, before anyone turns it.

outcomes.text: It belonged to the barrow's maker, who did not want it opened. He wrote down why, very carefully, in a hand that shook.

options.label: Leave it hanging. A key made of a finger is not an invitation.

outcomes.text: Though there is no wind, it sways after you as you go, like a finger beckoning.
